rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw is circumstantial: they know this while bowing, meaning in humility, submission, and lowliness before God during prayer and almsgiving.
rows.anchor: الواو فيه للحال اي يعلمون ذلك في حال الركوع وهو الخشوع والإخبات والتواضع لله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes the circumstantial phrase with giving zakat: they give it while bowing in prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو حال من يؤتون الزكاة بمعنى يؤتونها في حال ركوعهم في الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the verse was revealed about ʿAlī, who gave a petitioner his ring while bowing; al-Zamakhsharī calls it baseless.
rows.anchor: 357 أنها نزلت في علي كرم الله وجهه حين سأله سائل وهو راكع في صلاته فطرح له خاتمه + باطل لا أصل له +

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story supposes the ring was on ʿAlī’s little finger, so removing it required no substantial movement that would invalidate prayer.
rows.anchor: كأنه كان مرجا في خنصره فلم يتكلف لخلعه كثير عما تفسد بمثله صلاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plural wording for a single reported occasion encourages others to imitate the act and attain its reward.
rows.anchor: جيء به على لفظ الجمع وإن كان السبب فيه رجلا واحدا ليرغب الناس في مثل فعله فينالوا مثل ثوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording also portrays believers as exceptionally eager for charity and attentive to the poor, not postponing urgent help even while praying.
rows.anchor: ولينبه على ان سجية المؤمنين يجب أن تكون على هذه الغاية من الحرص على البر والإحسان وتفقد الفقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit phrase حزب الله replaces a pronoun; the meaning is that they are the ones who prevail.
rows.anchor: من إقامة الظاهر مقام المضمر ومعناه فإنهم هم الغالبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming them God’s party marks their defining affiliation; ḥizb originally means a group assembled around its cause.
rows.anchor: ولكنهم بذلك جعلوا اعلاما لكونهم حزب الله وأصل الحزب القوم يجتمعون لأمر حزبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also allows حزب الله to refer specifically to the Messenger and the believers.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد بحزب الله الرسول والمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever takes them as patrons has thereby taken God’s party as patron and gained support from one none can overcome.
rows.anchor: ومن يتولهم فقد تولى حزب الله واعتضد بمن لا يغالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مكناكم means either that God gave people a settled place in the earth or made them its owners and able to act there.
rows.anchor: جعلنا لكم فيها مكانا وقرارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: معايش is the plural of معيشة: food, drink, other means of living, and the means by which they are obtained.
rows.anchor: وهي ما يعاش به من المطاعم والمشارب وغيرها

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: The preferred form has an explicit yāʾ; Ibn ʿĀmir reads it with hamza, by analogy with صحائف.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عامر : أنه همز ، على التشبيه بصحائف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلقناكم ثم صورناكم refers to creating Adam as unformed clay and then forming him; the following command to the angels confirms this sequence.
rows.anchor: يعني خلقنا أباكم آدم طينا غير مصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من الساجدين means among those who prostrated to Adam.
rows.anchor: من الساجدين } ممن سجد لآدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address يا آدم is explained as God saying to Adam, ‘O Adam.’
rows.anchor: وعلم ءادم } وقلنا : يا آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has هذي الشجرة; the original vowel is yāʾ, with hāʾ replacing it.
rows.anchor: هذي الشجرة ) والأصل الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وسوس means speaking secretly with repetition; the same form describes jewelry making a soft sound, and it is intransitive like the cited verbs.
rows.anchor: إذا تكلم كلاما خفيا يكرره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive participle is موسوس with a kasra on wāw, not a fatḥa; one says موسوس له or إليه for the person receiving the whisper.
rows.anchor: ورجل موسوس بكسر الواو ولا يقال موسوس بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making their nakedness appear was Satan’s aim, so they would be distressed at seeing exposed what they wished to cover.
rows.anchor: جعل ذلك غرضا له ليسوءهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage shows that exposing nakedness is a grave matter, always repugnant to natural taste and reason.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن كشف العورة من عظائم الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second wāw in ووري is a long vowel like the alif in وارى, so the rounded wāw does not change to hamza as in أو يصل.
rows.anchor: لأن الثانية مدة كألف وارى

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh has the hamza-substituted reading أورى.
rows.anchor: قراءة عبد الله : ( أورى ) بالقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception expresses fear that the two might become angels; the passage suggests angelhood is the higher form toward which human nature looks.
rows.anchor: إلا كراهة أن تكونا ملكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has malakayn with kasra on the lām, as in the phrase in 20:120.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( ملكين ) بكسر اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The immortals are those who do not die and remain dwelling in the Garden.
rows.anchor: من الذين لا يموتون ويبقون في الجنة ساكنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two variants are noted: من سوأتهما with the singular, and وسواتهما with a geminated wāw.
rows.anchor: من سوأتهما ) ، بالتوحيد ، ( وسواتهما ) ، بالواو المشددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although qāsamah ordinarily means mutual oath-taking, it can mean Satan swore to them and they answered, he swore sincerely and they accepted, or his effort was like that of a partner in oath-taking.
rows.anchor: كأنه قال لهما : أقسم لكما إني لمن الناصحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فدلاهما means that he brought the pair down to eating from the tree.
rows.anchor: فنزلهما إلى الأكل من الشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their deception consisted of Satan’s oath by God.
rows.anchor: بما غرهما به من القسم بالله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the believer is deceived only by invoking God.
rows.anchor: قتادة : وإنما يخدع المؤمن بالله

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar freed servants for obedience and good prayer; when told they performed these acts to win freedom, he said he accepts being deceived through God.
rows.anchor: ابن عمر رضي الله عنه : أنه كان إذا رأى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They tasted the tree in the sense that they began eating from it.
rows.anchor: وجدا طعمها آخذين في الأكل منها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Two identifications are transmitted for the forbidden tree: an ear of grain or a grapevine.
rows.anchor: قيل : الشجرة هي السنبلة . وقيل : شجرة الكرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their clothing fell away and their nakedness became visible, although they had not seen it on themselves or on each other before.
rows.anchor: أي تهافت عنهما اللباس فظهرت لهما عوراتهما

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha is cited saying, ‘I did not see his, nor he mine,’ in the discussion of the pair’s clothing and nakedness.
rows.anchor: ما رأيت منه ولا رأى مني

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr says their clothing was of the same kind as fingernails.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير : كان لباسهما من جنس الأظفار

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says their clothing was light that kept them from seeing one another.
rows.anchor: وهب : كان لباسهما نورا يحول بينهما وبين النظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طفق means that someone began doing something.
rows.anchor: طفق بفعل كذا ، بمعنى جعل يفعل كذا

rows.speaker: أبو السمال
rows.claim: Abū al-Sammāl reads وطفقا with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: أبو السمال : ( وطفقا ) بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They layered leaves over their nakedness to cover it, like patching a shoe with successive layers fastened by straps.
rows.anchor: ورقة فوق ورقة على عوراتهما ليستترا بها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads يخصفان with kasra on khāʾ and a doubled ṣād, from يختصفان.
rows.anchor: الحسن : ( يخصفان ) بكسر الخاء وتشديد الصاد

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī reads يخصفان from أخصف, a causative form derived from خصف: they cover themselves.
rows.anchor: من أخصف ، وهو منقول من خصف أي يخصفان أنفسهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading derives يخصفان from the doubled form خصف.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( يخصفان ) من خصف بالتشديد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The leaves of the Garden are identified as fig leaves.
rows.anchor: قيل : كان ورق التين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s words rebuke and admonish them, drawing attention to their failure to guard against Satan’s hostility.
rows.anchor: عتاب من الله تعالى وتوبيخ وتنبيه على الخطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report has God ask whether the Garden’s many trees were not enough; Adam admits this but says he never expected a creature to swear falsely by God. God then sends them down to a life of toil, and Adam learns ironwork and farming.
rows.anchor: روي : أنه قال لآدم : ألم يكن لك فيما منحتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelieving chiefs address those below them, trying to dissuade them from believing in Shuʿayb.
rows.anchor: أي أشرافهم للذين دونهم يثبطونهم عن الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call following Shuʿayb a loss because it exchanges error for guidance, as in the description in 2:16.
rows.anchor: لاستبدالكم الضلالة بالهدى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says they would lose the gains of fraud and short measure, since Shuʿayb forbids these and demands full, even measure.
rows.anchor: قيل : تخسرون باتباعه فوائد البخس والتطفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنكم إذا لخاسرون supplies both the answer to the oath introduced by the lām and the answer to the condition.
rows.anchor: إنكم إذا لخاسرون } ساد مسد الجوابين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الذين كذبوا شعيبا is a subject whose predicate is كأن لم يغنوا فيها; the repeated clause likewise has كانوا هم الخاسرين as its predicate.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ خبره { كأن لم يغنوا فيها } وكذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening gives exclusive focus: Shuʿayb’s deniers alone were annihilated as if they had never lived there, while his followers were saved; they alone suffered the great loss.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا الابتداء معنى الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resumptive opening and repetition emphatically refute the chiefs’ claim, disparage their judgment, mock their advice, and magnify their people’s fate.
rows.anchor: مبالغة في رد مقالة الملإ لأشياعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God dispersed the Israelites across the earth as separate peoples, so few lands lack a group of them.
rows.anchor: وفرقناهم فيها ، فلا يكاد يخلوا بلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous are identified either as those among them who believed in Medina or as those living beyond China.
rows.anchor: الذين آمنوا منهم بالمدينة ، أو الذين وراء الصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those ‘below that’ are people lower than the righteous in standing: unbelievers and sinners.
rows.anchor: منهم ناس دون ذلك الوصف منحطون عنه ، وهم الكفرة والفسقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دون ذلك is nominative as an adjective of an omitted noun, meaning ‘people lower than that’; the same construction appears in 37:164.
rows.anchor: الرفع ، وهو صفة لموصوف محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good and bad things are blessings and afflictions by which God tested them.
rows.anchor: بلوناهم بالحسنات والسيئات } بالنعم والنقم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The aim is that they stop their wrongdoing and repent.
rows.anchor: النقم { لعلهم } ينتهون فينيبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later generation consists of people in the Prophet’s time who inherited the Torah, read its commands, prohibitions, and rulings, but did not act on them.
rows.anchor: من بعد المذكورين { خلف } وهم الذين كانوا في زمن رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عرض هذا الأدنى is the perishable goods of this near or lowly world; the phrasing belittles it, and the people took bribes in judgments to alter wording for commoners.
rows.anchor: أي حطام هذا الشيء الأدنى ، يريد الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الأدنى can derive from nearness, since worldly gain is immediate, or from low rank, baseness, and smallness.
rows.anchor: الأدنى : إما من الدنو بمعنى القرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They assume God will not hold them to account for what they took and will forgive them.
rows.anchor: لا يؤاخذنا الله بما أخذنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase لنا is the grammatical subject of يغفر; it may alternatively be the verbal noun of يأخذون, ‘the taking.’
rows.anchor: وفاعل { سيغفر } الجار والمجرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw is circumstantial: they welcome forgiveness while persisting and returning to the same act without repentance.
rows.anchor: مصرون عائدون إلى مثل فعلهم ، غير تائبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness of sins requires repentance; a person persisting in sin is not forgiven.
rows.anchor: وغفران الذنوب لا يصح إلا بالتوبة ، والمصر لا غفران له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant refers to the Torah’s rule that a grave sin is forgiven only through repentance.
rows.anchor: من ارتكب ذنبا عظيما فإنه لا يغفر له إلا بالتوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They had studied the Book’s condition that forgiveness requires repentance.
rows.anchor: في الكتاب من اشتراط التوبة في غفران الذنوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī polemically says the doctrine of the determinists is exactly the Jews’ doctrine described here.
rows.anchor: والذي عليه المجبرة هو مذهب اليهود بعينه كما ترى

rows.speaker: مالك بن دينار
rows.claim: Mālik b. Dīnār warns of people who fall short then presume forgiveness because they avoided polytheism; he calls their attitude wishful thinking and says even their best are complacent, like the people in this verse.
rows.anchor: وعن مالك بن دينار رحمه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is better than that paltry worldly gain for those who avoid bribes and God’s prohibitions.
rows.anchor: والدار الاخرة خير } من ذلك العرض الخسيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source lists variants including ورثوا الكتاب, a tāʾ form for إلا تقولوا, وادارسوا meaning تدارسوا, and أفلا تعقلون with yāʾ or tāʾ.
rows.anchor: ورثوا الكتاب ) ، وإلا تقولوا ، بالتاء

words: أَن لَّا يَقُولُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْحَقَّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن لا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق can explain ميثاق الكتاب as an apposition: the covenant stated in the Book; claiming forgiveness without repentance then violates it and invents against God.
rows.anchor: هو عطف بيان لميثاق الكتاب

words: أَن لَّا يَقُولُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْحَقَّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the covenant means the earlier stipulation, أن لا يقولوا may be its purpose, ‘so they would not say,’ or أن may explain a prohibition: ‘Do not say about God except the truth.’
rows.anchor: وإن فسر ميثاق الكتاب بما تقدم ذكره كان { أن لا يقولوا } مفعولا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ودرسوا ما فيه coordinates with ألم يؤخذ عليهم: the covenant was taken from them and they studied its contents.
rows.anchor: على { ألم يؤخذ عليهم } ، لأنه تقرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols are treated as rational beings in وهم يخلقون because their worshippers believe in them and call them gods.
rows.anchor: أجريت الأصنام مجرى أولي العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One argument asks how people associate what cannot create as God does, when the worshippers themselves are created by God.
rows.anchor: أيشركون ما لا يقدر على خلق شيء كما يخلق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, idols are inert and cannot fabricate anything, while their worshippers make them, leaving the idols even less capable than their worshippers.
rows.anchor: أو لا يقدر على اختلاق شيء ، لأنه جماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols cannot protect their worshippers or themselves from harm; their worshippers are the ones who defend and protect the idols.
rows.anchor: بل عبدتهم هم الذي يدفعون عنهم ويحامون عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the idols to guidance, or asking them to guide and grant good as one asks God, brings no response or fulfillment.
rows.anchor: لا يتبعوكم إلى مرادكم وطلبتكم ، ولا يجيبوكم كما يجيبكم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the idols or remaining silent makes no difference: neither course brings success through them.
rows.anchor: أم صمتم عن دعائهم ، في أنه لا فلاح معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal construction presents silence as their usual state: in distress they call God, not idols, so initiating an invocation leaves their habitual silence unchanged; see 30:33.
rows.anchor: لأنهم كانوا إذا حزبهم أمر دعوا الله دون أصنامهم

words: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تدعون means worshipping them and naming them gods besides God.
rows.anchor: أي تعبدونهم وتسمونهم آلهة من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase mocks the idols: even if they were living and rational, they would merely be servants like their worshippers, with no superiority; the next questions deny they can act like people.
rows.anchor: استهزاء بهم ، أي قصارى أمرهم أن يكونوا أحياء عقلاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes عباد أمثالكم to mean that the idols are owned or subjected, as you are.
rows.anchor: وقيل : عباد أمثالكم مملوكون أمثالكم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr reads إن lightly and عبادا in the accusative: ‘Those you invoke are not servants like you’; إن works like the negative ما of Hijazi Arabic.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير : ( إن الذين تدعون من دون الله عبادا أمثالكم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He challenges them to summon their partners for help against him and plot together without delay; only one confident of God’s protection could speak this way, since they had threatened him with their idols.
rows.anchor: استعينوا بهم في عدوني { ثم كيدون } جميعا أنتم وشركاؤكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge echoes Hūd’s response after his people claimed their gods had harmed him: he declared himself free of their gods and challenged them to plot without delay.
rows.anchor: قوم هود له : { إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض ءالهتنا بسوء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God inwardly covers every kind of remembrance: Qurʾān recitation, supplication, glorification, tahlīl, and more.
rows.anchor: هو عام في الأذكار من قراءة القرآن والدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two words mean that the worshipper is humble and fearful.
rows.anchor: تضرعا وخيفة } متضرعا وخائفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speak below the level of public recitation; concealment deepens sincerity and better supports reflection.
rows.anchor: ومتكلما كلاما دون الجهر ، لأن الإخفاء أدخل في الإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may single out these two especially virtuous times or indicate continual remembrance; ghuduww means the morning hours.
rows.anchor: لفضل هذين الوقتين . أو أراد الدوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has والإيصال, from آصل ‘to enter the evening’; it parallels الغدو.
rows.anchor: الإيصال ) ، من آصل إذا دخل في الأصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heedless are those who neglect remembering God and occupy themselves with distractions.
rows.anchor: من الذين يغفلون عن ذكر الله ويلهون عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those near their Lord are the angels; ‘near’ means nearness in rank and closeness to God’s mercy and favor through their obedience and pursuit of His pleasure.
rows.anchor: هم الملائكة صلوات الله عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They reserve worship exclusively for God and associate no one with Him, implicitly rebuking other morally responsible beings.
rows.anchor: ويختصونه بالعبادة لا يشركون به غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet promises that reciting Sūrat al-Aʿrāf will place a screen between the reciter and Iblīs on Judgment Day, with Adam interceding for the reciter.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase denies that the hypocrites are believers, refutes their oath that they belong to the believers, and confirms the statement that they are not of them.
rows.anchor: أريد به نفي أن يكونوا من المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their conduct is the opposite of believers’: they command unbelief and sins and forbid faith and obedience.
rows.anchor: الكفر والمعاصي { وينهون عن المعروف } عن الإيمان والطاعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They hold back their hands out of greed, refusing goods, charity, and spending in God’s cause.
rows.anchor: عن الإيمان والطاعات { ويقبضون أيديهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They neglected God’s remembrance, so He left them without His mercy and favor.
rows.anchor: أغفلوا ذكره { فنسيهم } فتركهم من رحمته وفضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are complete in fisq: rebellion in unbelief and stripping themselves of every good.
rows.anchor: هم الكاملون في الفسق الذي هو التمرد في الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims should be deterred from earning this ugly name, which God uses in emphatic condemnation; the Prophet even disliked a Muslim saying ‘I am lazy,’ since hypocrites are called lazy in 4:142.
rows.anchor: وكفى المسلم زاجرا أن يلم بما يكسبه هذا الاسم الفاحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers’ mutual alliance contrasts with the hypocrites’ being ‘some from some’ in 9:67.
rows.anchor: في مقابلة قوله في المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future particle assures that mercy will certainly come; as with a future threat, it means the addressee cannot escape even if it is delayed, as also in 19:96, 93:5, and 4:152.
rows.anchor: السين مفيدة وجود الرحمة لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzīz means overpowering all and able to reward or punish; ḥakīm means placing everything where it belongs according to its due.
rows.anchor: غالب على كل شيء قادر عليه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the good dwellings as palaces of pearl, red ruby, and emerald.
rows.anchor: الحسن : قصورا من اللؤلؤ والياقوت الأحمر والزبرجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عَدْن is a proper name, supported by the wording in 19:61.
rows.anchor: و { عدن } علم ، بدليل قوله

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ reports from the Prophet that ʿAdn is God’s unseen abode, inhabited only by prophets, the truthful, and martyrs, and that God blesses whoever enters it; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: ما روى أبو الدرداء رضي الله عنه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other identifications call ʿAdn either a city in Paradise or a river with its gardens along the banks.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي مدينة في الجنة . وقيل : نهر جناته على حافاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s approval surpasses every gift: it causes success and happiness, brings honor, and makes other blessings enjoyable; awareness of His displeasure would spoil their pleasure.
rows.anchor: لأن رضاه هو سبب كل فوز وسعادة

rows.speaker: بعض أولى الهمة البعيدة والنفس المرة من مشايخنا
rows.claim: A demanding elder among al-Zamakhsharī’s teachers said his greatest longing was for God’s approval and to be gathered among those rightly guided and pleasing to Him, more than for any promised Paradise reward.
rows.anchor: وسمعت بعض أولى الهمة البعيدة والنفس المرة من مشايخنا يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذلك points either to all God’s promised rewards or specifically to His approval; this alone is the great triumph, beyond what people ordinarily count as victory.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما وعد الله ، أو إلى الرضوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not make false excuses for staying behind but admitted their wrongdoing with regret; the three named are Abū Lubāba Marwān b. ʿAbd al-Mundhir, Aws b. Thaʿlaba, and Wadīʿa b. Ḥizām.
rows.anchor: أي لم يعتذروا من تخلفهم بالمعاذير الكاذبة كغيرهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative report says ten men were involved and seven tied themselves to mosque pillars, believing they were doomed; they vowed to remain bound until the Prophet released them, and he waited for revelation before freeing and excusing them.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ( 488 ) كانوا عشرة ، فسبعة منهم أوثقوا أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After release, the men offered the wealth that had kept them back as charity for purification; the Prophet said he had not been ordered to take it, then the instruction to take charity was revealed.
rows.anchor: فقالوا : يا رسول الله ، هذه أموالنا التي خلفتنا عنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good deed means going out for jihad and the other deed means staying behind.
rows.anchor: عملا صالحا } خروجا إلى الجهاد

rows.speaker: الحسن والكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Kalbī instead take the good deed as repentance and the bad deed as sin.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن وعن الكلبي : التوبة والإثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each deed is both mixed with and mixed into its counterpart, like saying ‘I mixed water and milk’; this differs from ‘I mixed water with milk,’ where only water is the mixed item.
rows.anchor: كل واحد منهما مخلوط ومخلوط به ؛ لأن المعنى خلط كل واحد منهما الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordinated construction can also be understood by analogy with ‘I sold a sheep, a sheep and a dirham,’ meaning a sheep for a dirham.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من قولهم : بعت الشاة شاة ودرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their repentance need not be separately stated: admitting their sins itself indicates repentance.
rows.anchor: إذا ذكر اعترافهم بذنوبهم ، وهو دليل على التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that Hūd brought no clear proof is a lie and denial, like Quraysh demanding a sign despite the Prophet’s many signs.
rows.anchor: كذب منهم وجحود ، كما قالت قريش لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عن قولك is circumstantial: they will not abandon their gods in response to Hūd’s words, and they do not consider people like themselves fit to believe him.
rows.anchor: حال من الضمير في تاركي آلهتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their words aim to extinguish Hūd’s hope that they will accept his call.
rows.anchor: وما يصح من أمثالنا أن يصدقوا مثلك فيما يدعوهم إليه
